From the Board's 'Data Files for the Election Results' page; published after the canvass, and the Board's results pages for the same election are headed 'Official'. Every figure is split into early voting, election day, mail-in (first and second canvass) and provisional; a precinct's total here is their sum (the 2020 file also prints it as Total Votes).
For in the vote columns, Against in the 'Against' columns.
gaps: President and Vice President of the United States

The Board's own publications disagree here, and each is stored as printed (the precinct rows from the precinct file, the totals from the results page): in Calvert County the Board's precinct file gives 'Other Write-Ins' 248 votes and its county file 247; in Calvert County the precinct file gives 'Other Write-Ins' 248 votes and the county's results page 247; the results page gives 'Other Write-Ins' 18,045 votes in all and the precinct file 18,046.
Elections that cities and towns run themselves

Most of Maryland's 157 cities and towns elect their officers at their own elections, run under their charters and apart from the State Board, many in spring or in odd years. Some vote on the same November day but run the election themselves, and their results are on each town's own site, not in the Board's files: Takoma Park (mayor and council, ranked choice) and Ocean City (mayor and council) among them. Cumberland's and Hagerstown's elections are run by the county boards and are here.
